title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to [-90.0, 0.0, -90.0] and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Next, draw a 2D sketch on a new face. In the first loop of this face, draw a single circle centered at coordinates [0.0221, 0.0221] with a radius of 0.0221. Apply a scaling factor of 0.0441 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled 2D sketch into 3D by rotating it using the Euler angles [-90.0, 0.0, -90.0] and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to generate the 3D model, ensuring that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. This operation will create a new solid body with a length of 0.044117647058823525, a width of 0.044117647058823525, and a height of 0.75. This completes the construction of the rounded cylindrical base.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the base of the cylinder
circle_center = (0.0221, 0.0221)
circle_radius = 0.0221

# Create the circle in the XY plane
r = r.center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the circle to create the cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75
r = r.extrude(extrude_depth)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
